name: Michigan
agency: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
permitAge: 14 years 9 months (Level 1 Learner's License), after Segment 1 of driver education (Segment 1 can start at 14 years 8 months). Adults 18+ never licensed get a Temporary Instruction Permit (TIP), valid 180 days.

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, before the driving skills test (30 hours, 2 at night, before Segment 2)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months at Level 1 (3 months before Segment 2)
teen.nightLimit: Level 2: no driving 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a parent/guardian or designated licensed adult 21+, for work or to/from work, or to/from an authorized activity
teen.passengerLimit: Level 2: no more than one passenger under 21, unless a parent/guardian or designated adult 21+ is in the car, the passengers are immediate family, or for work or an authorized activity
teen.phone: Kelsey's Law (MCL 257.602c): Level 1 and Level 2 drivers may not use a phone while driving except to report emergencies. General law (MCL 257.602b, since June 30, 2023): no driver may hold or use a phone while driving, including while stopped at a light or in traffic; fines $100 first, $250 after.

bac.adult: 0.08 (0.17 or more is the high-BAC offense) - MCL 257.625(1)
bac.under21: any bodily alcohol content: 0.02 up to 0.08, or any alcohol from drinking (zero tolerance) - MCL 257.625(6)

notes: Handbook: What Every Driver Must Know, October 2025 (SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), read in full 2026-10-09. Printed page = PDF page minus 14.
Level 1 drivers must be with a licensed parent/guardian or a designated licensed adult 21+ (with a signed letter from the parent), in the front seat (p5).
Level 2: age 16, Level 1 held 6 months, Segment 2, skills test, and 90 days with no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes (p5, p8). Hard-card holders advance automatically.
Level 3: age 17, Level 2 held 6 months, 12 consecutive months clean; automatic with parental authorization (p5).

Speed (p26): 70 mph max / 55 min on freeways unless posted; 55 mph on other streets and highways unless posted; 25 mph platted subdivisions and condo complexes; 15 mph mobile home parks; 45 mph posted work zones. 75 mph on at least 600 miles of freeway per MCL 257.627(17) (not in handbook).

Move over (p28): slow at least 10 mph below the posted limit and move over a lane if possible for stopped emergency vehicles, tow trucks, waste haulers, utility and road maintenance vehicles with lights on.
Left turn on red onto a one-way street (from a one-way or two-way street) after a full stop, yielding (p30); No Turn On Red sign forbids it (p44).
School bus (p28-29): stop at least 20 feet away; no need to stop on the other side of a highway divided by a barrier or median.
Insurance: no-fault; owners must carry personal protection insurance (PIP), property protection insurance and residual liability (MCL 500.3101). Not in the handbook.

Knowledge test: free at every SOS office; online version for 18+ ($6.50 fee, launched July 2025). Offered in many languages in electronic, paper or audio form, and foreign-language interpreters are allowed on written tests except CDL (p7, back cover). The handbook and michigan.gov do not state the number of questions or the pass mark; third-party sources conflict, so left null.
No official Spanish handbook found (michigan.gov/sos/language-services/spanish lists none).
